newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Daimler to help Kiev airport refit.
newsitem.headline: Daimler to help Kiev airport refit.

text.p: Germany's Daimler Benz Aerospace and Kiev International Boryspil airport have signed an agreement on resurfacing the second runaway at Ukraine's biggest airport which has been out of service for years, an aviation official said on Friday.
Mykola Deinega, who heads the airports division at the state aviation authority, said Daimler Benz would supply air traffic control equipment worth 185 million marks.
"There was no such money in the state budget. It will be financed with German credits with guarantees from the Ukrainian government," Deinega said of the deal, signed on Thursday.
"In the very near future we will announce a tender to choose the best builder for the runway," he added.
Deinega said work would be completed in 1998. Boryspil's second runway was built in the 1970s but shut several years ago.
More than 30 airlines, including most major European carriers, fly regularly into Boryspil, which itself underwent major renovations three years ago.
It operates with only one runway, which, Deinega said, would also be resurfaced but declined to give any details.

The runway problem was highlighted in 1995 when Boryspil was shut down for several hours to allow a plane carrying Ukraine's defence minister to make an emergency landing after it lost a wheel on take-off.
